text:
Christopher Columbus

The writing style described—characterized by puns, malapropisms, and a humorous, stage-performance-oriented tone—is highly indicative of **Groucho Marx**. Marx was famous for his rapid-fire wit, deliberate misuse of words (malapropisms), and wordplay, which were central to his act in the Marx Brothers films and his radio/television shows. The description of the text as a "candid reflection of the writer's humorous stage performances" aligns perfectly with Marx's public persona and comedic legacy.
